name: Dwarpal
author: Dwarpal

sections.description:
Dwarpal (Dwarpal WP Security Plugin) protects your WordPress site from common threats, including:

  • Firewall Protection – Automatically blocks malicious requests containing SQL injection, XSS, code injection, and directory traversal attempts
  • Login Security – Protects against brute force attacks by limiting login attempts and locking out suspicious IP addresses
  • SEO Hack Protection – Detects Thai/gambling spam, wp-config injectors, and bot cloaking via local User-Agent comparison (no Google scraping)
  • Bot View Scanner – Compares browser vs search-bot responses on your own site; scans wp-config.php and index.php for known malware signatures
  • Critical Options Monitor – Alerts when key WordPress settings (site URL, admin email, registration) are changed—catches takeover and redirect hacks
  • Outbound Request Monitor – Logs outbound HTTP requests from your site to detect backdoors and data exfiltration
  • Security Logging – Comprehensive audit log of all security events for monitoring and analysis
  • WordPress Hardening – Removes WordPress version information, disables XML-RPC, and implements other security best practices
  • Malware Scanning – Scans files for malware and suspicious patterns
  • File Integrity Monitoring – Monitors core files for unauthorized changes
  • Two-Factor Authentication – Adds an extra layer of security to login
  • IP Blocking & Whitelisting – Block malicious IPs and whitelist trusted ones
  • Live Traffic Monitoring – Real-time monitoring of website traffic
  • Vulnerability Scanner – Checks for known vulnerabilities in WordPress core, plugins, and themes
  • Threat Defense – Opt-in signature feed, virtual patches, auto-block reputation, and security digests
  • OWASP Coverage Report – Maps enabled controls to OWASP Top 10 categories

Features

Firewall

  • Real-time request scanning
  • Pattern-based threat detection
  • Automatic blocking of malicious requests
  • Configurable firewall rules

Login Security

  • Failed login attempt tracking
  • IP-based lockout system
  • Configurable attempt limits
  • Customizable lockout duration

Security Logging

  • Complete audit trail
  • Event type categorization
  • IP address tracking
  • Request URI logging
  • User agent recording

WordPress Hardening

  • WordPress version hiding
  • XML-RPC disabling
  • RSD link removal
  • File editing protection

External services

This plugin can optionally connect to third-party services only when you enable the related feature in the plugin settings. Features that call external services are off by default unless noted.

Google Safe Browsing / Transparency Report (blocklist monitoring)

  • What it is: A Google page used to check whether your domain appears to be flagged for unsafe browsing.
  • When it is called: Only when Blocklist Monitoring is enabled (disabled by default; requires opt-in).
  • What data is sent: Your site domain (host) is sent as part of the request URL.
  • Why: To help you identify if your domain may be flagged and needs remediation.
  • Service provider: Google.
  • Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms
  • Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

ip-api.com (GeoIP country lookup)

  • What it is: A GeoIP service used to map an IP address to a country code.
  • When it is called: Only when Geo-blocking is enabled.
  • What data is sent: The visitor IP address is sent to ip-api.com to determine the country code.
  • Why: To enforce country-based access restrictions when you enable geo-blocking.
  • Service provider: ip-api.com.
  • Terms: https://ip-api.com/docs/legal
  • Privacy: https://ip-api.com/docs/legal

Bot View Scanner (local cloaking detection)

  • What it is: A local scan that requests your own site URLs with different User-Agent headers (normal browser vs search bot) to detect cloaking.
  • When it is called: Only when you click Run Bot View Scan or enable Daily Bot View Scan in SEO Protection settings.
  • What data is sent: HTTP requests are made to your own site (home_url()). No data is sent to Google or third-party search engines.
  • Why: To detect SEO cloaking and wp-config/index.php injection patterns seen in real server compromises.
  • External link: Google Search Console is linked for manual verification only (opens in your browser; the plugin does not scrape Google).

WordPress.org API (vulnerability scanner)

  • What it is: Official WordPress.org endpoints for core/plugin version data.
  • When it is called: When you run the vulnerability scanner.
  • What data is sent: Plugin slugs and WordPress version identifiers (standard update API usage).
  • Service provider: WordPress.org.
  • Terms: https://wordpress.org/about/gpl/
  • Privacy: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/

Optional signature feed (Threat Defense)

  • What it is: JSON feed of firewall, malware, and virtual-patch signatures.
  • When it is called: Only when Signature feed sync is enabled. If no URL is set, the plugin refreshes from its bundled data/signatures.json. If you set a remote URL, that URL is fetched daily (or on demand).
  • What data is sent: A normal HTTPS GET to your configured feed URL. No site visitor data is included.
  • Why: To keep detection rules updatable without waiting for a full plugin release.
  • Important: Leave disabled (default) if you do not want outbound feed requests.

Optional IP reputation lookup (Threat Defense)

  • What it is: An optional JSON reputation endpoint you configure yourself.
  • When it is called: Only when local auto-block and remote reputation lookup are both enabled and a reputation URL is set.
  • What data is sent: The visitor IP address as a query parameter.
  • Expected response: JSON such as {"block":true,"score":90}.
  • Important: Disabled by default. Do not enable unless you understand and trust the endpoint you configure.

WordPress.org compliance (storage)

Database exports and plugin-generated files are stored only under:

wp-content/uploads/dwarpal/

This plugin does not:
– Copy or modify wp-config.php
– Write .htaccess to wp-content/ or WordPress core directories
– Define DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT globally (file editor is disabled via a setting + capability filter)
– Call remote files for CSS/JS/images (all assets are bundled)
sections.installation:
1. Upload the dwarpal folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress
  3. Navigate to ‘Dwarpal’ in the WordPress admin menu to configure settings
sections.faq:
What security features does Dwarpal provide?

Dwarpal provides firewall protection, login security, security logging, and WordPress hardening features.

Does Dwarpal affect site performance?

Dwarpal is designed to be lightweight and efficient. Security checks are performed early in the WordPress loading process to minimize performance impact.

Can I customize the firewall rules?

Yes, firewall rules can be customized through the admin interface. Additional customization options may be available in future versions.

How does the login security work?

The login security system tracks failed login attempts by IP address. After a configurable number of failed attempts, the IP address is temporarily locked out.
sections.changelog:
1.2.19

  • Requires WordPress 5.3+. Outbound allow-list no longer trips Plugin Check offloading

1.2.18

  • Plugin Check: nonce and REQUEST_URI sanitization warnings cleared on firewall and traffic logging

1.2.17

  • Live Traffic screen reads 30 short rows and stops logging once the table is full

1.2.16

  • Live traffic no longer stores every bot 404, and the traffic screen reads only the latest rows

1.2.15

  • Firewall no longer blocks a normal page that contains an embed. IP lookups and media previews are not security events

1.2.14

  • Live traffic and security logs show the server clock

1.2.13

  • Security log times follow the site clock. Viewing a page is not logged as an SEO hack

1.2.12

  • Firewall matches SQL injection, XSS, code injection, and directory traversal in the raw URL and in public form posts

1.2.11

  • Fix: viewing a normal page is no longer logged as an SEO hack attempt

1.2.10

  • Fix: live traffic records the real HTTP status. Missing pages were stored as 200

1.2.9

  • Fix: activation no longer alters existing log tables, which timed out and returned Internal Server Error on large sites

1.2.8

  • Fix: dashboard and scans no longer run COUNT(*) on the log tables
  • Fix: HTTP errors, traffic and security logs are trimmed on a schedule (7 or 30 days)
  • Fix: admin pages, plugin update checks and image requests are not written to the logs

1.2.7

  • Fix: malware, integrity, vulnerability and update checks no longer start during the first page view after activation

1.2.6

  • Fix: log tables use InnoDB, and old traffic rows are deleted in small scheduled batches, so page views no longer lock the tables

1.2.5

  • Activation: database tables created with dbDelta (versioned schema, multisite aware); no output or external requests on activation
  • Admin CSS/JS load only on Dwarpal screens
  • File and directory locations resolved with WordPress functions; the plugin no longer deletes core files (readme.html removal option replaced by a server block rule)
  • Vulnerability scan uses WordPress core update data instead of contacting external servers
  • Fix: file integrity baseline is built in time-limited batches (no timeout on large or slow sites)
  • Fix: update alerts and other scheduled tasks load required WordPress admin functions before use
  • Fix: uninstall now removes plugin tables, options and scheduled events
  • Fix: PHP warnings on the dashboard and on Firewall / 2FA settings save; 404s no longer logged twice
  • Fix: “404 Exploit Attempt” is logged only for real 404 responses (admin pages and admin-ajax requests were reported as attacks)

1.2.3

  • Security: capability checks on all admin screens and pending-user approve/reject
  • Security: nonce verification on 2FA profile save
  • Fix: approving a pending user no longer triggers a fatal error

1.2.2

  • Plugin Check cleanup: text domain set to dwarpal to match plugin slug/folder
  • Removed Google hostname string patterns that falsely triggered Offloading checks
  • Removed debug error_log(); hardened nonce/sanitize handling and DB query annotations
  • readme: Tested up to 7.1; shortened short description

1.2.1

  • Plugin display name set to Dwarpal; description set to Dwarpal WP Security Plugin
  • WordPress.org review hardening: sanitization, escaping, opt-in external services, uploads-only storage
  • Text domain remains dwarpal to match the directory slug

1.2.0

  • Threat Defense: opt-in updatable signature/rule feed (bundled or remote JSON)
  • Virtual patches for known vulnerable plugin request patterns (no file overwrites)
  • OWASP Top 10 coverage mapping and admin report
  • Opt-in smarter auto-block with local reputation scoring and optional remote lookup
  • Daily/weekly security alerting digests (email)

1.1.1

  • Centralized backup storage under uploads/dwarpal/ via WP_Filesystem
  • Removed wp-config.php copies and wp-content/.htaccess writes
  • File editor disable uses capability filter only (no DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT constant)
  • Hardening PHP-block options are recommendations with copy-paste Apache rules
  • Backup protection uses firewall rules only (no .htaccess modification)
  • Fixed remaining text domain strings for plugin slug compliance

1.1.0

  • Bot View Scanner: local cloaking detection (browser vs bot User-Agent) — replaces non-compliant Google search scraping
  • SEO signatures from real incidents: eval/base64, web shells, Thai SEO APIs, mass-injection markers
  • Daily core file scan (wp-config.php, index.php) with admin alerts
  • Blocklist monitoring remains opt-in (disabled by default)

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Firewall protection
  • Login security features
  • Security logging
  • WordPress hardening
  • Admin interface
